rationale: This is a one-slot substitution into the archived "Maturity-Wall Gross Profit Trend" (identical RANK(dlc/lt)×RANK(lt/at) gate, with a COGS-intensity trend replacing the gross-profit asset-yield trend already tested there and in "Working-Capital Gross Margin Squeeze"), i.e., a cosmetic variant of an existing hit rather than a new mechanism.

This is the archived "Current-Claim Gross Profit Buffer" with dltt merely added to the denominator — a pure scaling tweak that adds no new economic content and remains largely a gross-profitability-times-inverse-leverage restatement.

The hypothesis, inputs, and expected sign are identical to the archived "Interest-Stressed Margin Harvesting," with only the MUL→MIN aggregation change that was already exercised in the "Cost-Stickiness Bottleneck" experiment, so it re-tests a known result rather than a new mechanism.

The conjunctive construction is internally consistent with the negative expected sign and the operating-vs-net-income disconnect under leverage is a defensible distinct mechanism, though it overlaps materially with the well-known low-ROA/financial-distress anomaly and with the archived "Levered Profit-Equity Disconnect," so incremental information is uncertain.

It is a slot-swap of the already-failed "Gross-Funded Liability Paydown" (same RANK(gross-profit trend)×RANK(dlc/lt) gate, with Δwcap replacing Δlt), and the base term NEG(Δwcap/at) is essentially the published working-capital accrual anomaly, making this both derivative and a partial rediscovery.

This merely flips the profitability conditioner of the archived "Profitable Maturity-Wall R&D Retrenchment" while keeping the same negative expected sign, and the archive's "Unfunded R&D Loss Pressure" result (positive alpha t=3.15 for distressed R&D intensity) argues the sign for loss-firm R&D cuts should plausibly be the opposite of what is claimed.
